before.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

before.supportingExcerpt: How CRS is graded, from the ASTCT 2019 consensus. The definition requires a fever of 38 degrees Celsius or higher that cannot be attributed to another cause. Severity is then the more severe of two findings, again not attributable to another cause. Grade 1 has neither. Grade 2 is low blood pressure that does not need vasopressors and/or oxygen by low-flow nasal cannula (up to 6 litres a minute) or blow-by. Grade 3 is one vasopressor, with or without vasopressin, and/or high-flow cannula, face mask, non-rebreather mask or Venturi mask. Grade 4 is multiple vasopressors, excluding vasopressin, and/or positive pressure such as CPAP, BiPAP or intubation. Once someone has had a fever-lowering or anti-cytokine treatment such as tocilizumab or steroids, fever is no longer needed to grade later severity: the grade then follows blood pressure and oxygen, and the person still counts as having CRS until the signs resolve. Organ toxicities linked to CRS are graded separately and do not change the CRS grade, and neurotoxicity during or after CRS is scored on the neurotoxicity scale, not added here. The 2026 ASTCT update (Perales et al.) convened experts to consider updating CRS, ICANS and haemophagocytic-lymphohistiocytosis-like grading, but only its abstract could be read, so whether it keeps, changes or relaxes any of these 2019 rules is not stated here; a report should say which version graded it.

CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. before.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

before.supportingExcerpt: How CRS is graded, from the ASTCT 2019 consensus. The definition requires a fever of 38 degrees Celsius or higher that cannot be attributed to another cause. Severity is then the more severe of two findings, again not attributable to another cause. Grade 1 has neither. Grade 2 is low blood pressure that does not need vasopressors and/or oxygen by low-flow nasal cannula (up to 6 litres a minute) or blow-by. Grade 3 is one vasopressor, with or without vasopressin, and/or high-flow cannula, face mask, non-rebreather mask or Venturi mask. Grade 4 is multiple vasopressors, excluding vasopressin, and/or positive pressure such as CPAP, BiPAP or intubation. Once someone has had a fever-lowering or anti-cytokine treatment such as tocilizumab or steroids, fever is no longer needed to grade later severity: the grade then follows blood pressure and oxygen, and the person still counts as having CRS until the signs resolve. Organ toxicities linked to CRS are graded separately and do not change the CRS grade, and neurotoxicity during or after CRS is scored on the neurotoxicity scale, not added here. The 2026 ASTCT update (Perales et al.) convened experts to consider updating CRS, ICANS and haemophagocytic-lymphohistiocytosis-like grading, but only its abstract could be read, so whether it keeps, changes or relaxes any of these 2019 rules is not stated here; a report should say which version graded it.

In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.
